claims.text: A controlled, moderate aging heat treatment will induce a uniform dispersion of nanoscale coherent precipitates in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The aging-induced precipitates will improve the strength–plasticity combination relative to the as-cast or as-homogenized state.
The proposed initial material is a single-phase refractory high-entropy alloy, such as one with a BCC structure.
An intermediate-temperature aging treatment can precipitate a fine coherent secondary phase.
Optimizing aging temperature and duration can avoid precipitate coarsening or overaging.
Coherent precipitates act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion enhances alloy strength.
Coherent precipitates act as sites for dislocation nucleation.
Dislocation nucleation at coherent precipitates promotes ductility.
The aged alloy will have a statistically significant increase in yield strength relative to an untreated as-cast or as-homogenized control.
The aged alloy will maintain or modestly improve ductility relative to the untreated control.
Improvement requires an optimal precipitate volume fraction, size, and spatial distribution.
Improper aging temperature or duration may cause overaging or embrittlement.
The magnitude of strength and ductility changes will depend on aging parameters and alloy composition.
